title: Letters Written during a Trip to Southern India & Ceylon in the Winter of 1876–1877
publisher: Printed by C. Roworth & Sons, for private circulation
summary: After thirty-five years of professional life in London, Charles Reynolds Williams went in the winter of 1876–77 with his brother, Monier Williams, the Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford, on a tour of western and southern India, and wrote these letters home as he travelled. They sail from Southampton by the Suez Canal to Bombay, go north by rail to Baroda and Ahmedabad in Gujarat, then by Poona and Mahabaleshwar to Madras, up to Ootacamund in the Nilgiris, and south by Tanjore, Trichinopoly and Madura to Ramnad, Tuticorin and Tinnevelly, and across to Ceylon. Williams returns alone by a coasting steamer along the Malabar coast to Bombay, visits Ellora with his brother, and stops at Cairo on the way home. The book was printed for his family and friends, with lithographs of his own sketches.
